name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Microsporangium wall layers microsporogenesis and pollen anatomy

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding the male reproductive structures in flowering plants:

Statement I: A typical angiosperm anther is a tetragonal structure consisting of four microsporangia situated at the corners, two in each lobe.

Statement II: The outer three wall layers—epidermis, endothecium, and middle layers—function in protection and dehiscence of the anther.

Statement III: The tapetum is the innermost wall layer that provides nourishment to the developing pollen grains.

Statement IV: Tapetal cells undergo meiotic reduction division to generate microspore tetrads directly.

Statement V: The exine layer of the pollen grain is composed of sporopollenin, which is absent at the germ pores.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे पुष्पी पादपों में नर जनन संरचनाओं के संबंध में पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक प्रारूपिक आवृतबीजी परागकोश एक चतुष्कोणीय संरचना होती है जिसके कोनों पर चार लघुबीजाणुधानियां स्थित होती हैं, प्रत्येक पालि में दो।

कथन II: बाहरी तीन भित्ति परतें—बाह्यत्वचा, अंतस्थीसियम और मध्य परतें—परागकोश की सुरक्षा और प्रस्फुटन में कार्य करती हैं।

कथन III: टेपिटम सबसे भीतरी भित्ति परत है जो विकासशील परागकणों को पोषण प्रदान करती है।

कथन IV: टेपिटम कोशिकाएं लघुबीजाणु चतुष्क उत्पन्न करने के लिए प्रत्यक्ष रूप से अर्धसूत्री विभाजन करती हैं।

कथन V: परागकण का बाह्यचोल स्पोरोपोलेनिन से बना होता है, जो जनन छिद्रों पर अनुपस्थित होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding tetragonal anther organization
An angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe containing two microsporangia, conferring a four-cornered tetragonal cross-sectional profile. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding the outer three wall layers
The epidermis, endothecium with its fibrous thickenings, and middle layers work synergistically to protect the sporogenous tissue and rupture along the line of dehiscence at maturity. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding tapetum function
The innermost tapetal tissue lines the sporangial cavity, synthesizing nutritive reserves, enzymes, and sporopollenin precursors to feed maturing microspores. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding tapetal meiosis
Microspores originate exclusively from meiotic divisions of diploid sporogenous cells (pollen mother cells). Tapetal cells do not divide meiotically to form spores; instead, they function solely as somatic nutritive support. Therefore, attributing meiotic spore formation to the tapetum is scientifically inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding sporopollenin and germ pores
The sculptured exine is composed of chemically inert sporopollenin, but displays localized circular apertures (germ pores) devoid of sporopollenin through which the pollen tube emerges. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Conclusion:
The claims regarding tetragonal morphology, outer layer protection, tapetal nutrition, and exine germ pore structure are valid, whereas the claim asserting tapetal meiosis is invalid. Thus, the first, second, third, and fifth claims are correct while the fourth claim is incorrect.

चरण 1: परागकोश की चतुष्कोणीय संरचना का मूल्यांकन
आवृतबीजी परागकोश द्विपालित और चतुष्कोणीय होता है, जिसके चारों कोनों पर दो-दो करके कुल चार लघुबीजाणुधानियां स्थित होती हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 2: बाहरी तीन भित्ति परतों की भूमिका का मूल्यांकन
बाह्यत्वचा, अंतस्थीसियम और मध्य परतें विकासशील ऊतकों की सुरक्षा करती हैं तथा परिपक्वता पर परागकोश के प्रस्फुटन में सहायता करती हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 3: टेपिटम के पोषण संबंधी कार्य का मूल्यांकन
सबसे भीतरी परत टेपिटम विकासशील परागकणों को आवश्यक पोषक तत्व प्रदान करने का कार्य करती है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 4: टेपिटम में अर्धसूत्री विभाजन का मूल्यांकन
लघुबीजाणुओं का निर्माण बीजाणुजन ऊतक (पराग मातृ कोशिकाओं) में अर्धसूत्री विभाजन से होता है, टेपिटम से नहीं। टेपिटम केवल पोषण प्रदान करता है। अतः टेपिटम में अर्धसूत्री विभाजन का दावा असत्य है।

चरण 5: स्पोरोपोलेनिन तथा जनन छिद्रों का मूल्यांकन
बाह्यचोल स्पोरोपोलेनिन से बना होता है, परंतु जनन छिद्रों पर स्पोरोपोलेनिन अनुपस्थित होता है ताकि पराग नली बाहर निकल सके। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

निष्कर्ष:
चतुष्कोणीय संरचना, सुरक्षात्मक भित्ति परतों, टेपिटम के पोषण कार्य तथा जनन छिद्रों से संबंधित विवरण सही हैं, जबकि टेपिटम द्वारा अर्धसूत्री विभाजन से बीजाणु निर्माण का विवरण गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and V are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect
Statements I, II, IV, and V are correct, but Statement III is incorrect
Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct, but Statement I is incorrect
All Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Ovule anatomy megasporogenesis and female gametophyte development

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding ovule architecture and female gametophyte development in angiosperms:

Statement I: The ovule is attached to the placenta by a stalk called the funicle, and the junction where the ovule fuses with the funicle is the hilum.

Statement II: The protective integuments encircle the nucellar tissue completely, leaving no terminal opening at all.

Statement III: A single diploid megaspore mother cell differentiates in the micropylar region of the nucellus and undergoes meiotic division.

Statement IV: Monosporic development describes the formation of an embryo sac from a single functional megaspore following degeneration of the remaining three.

Statement V: A typical mature female gametophyte (embryo sac) in angiosperms is 8-nucleate and 7-celled.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे आवृतबीजी पादपों में बीजांड की संरचना तथा मादा युग्मकोद्भिद् के विकास के संबंध में पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: बीजांड एक वृंत द्वारा अपरा से जुड़ा होता है जिसे बीजांडवृंत कहते हैं, तथा वह संधि जहां बीजांड बीजांडवृंत से संलयित होता है, नाभिका कहलाती है।

कथन II: सुरक्षात्मक अध्यावरण बीजांडकाय को पूरी तरह से घेरे रहते हैं, जिससे शीर्ष पर कोई छिद्र या निकास शेष नहीं रहता है।

कथन III: बीजांडकाय के बीजांडद्वारीय क्षेत्र में एक एकल द्विगुणित गुरुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिका विभेदित होकर अर्धसूत्री विभाजन करती है।

कथन IV: एकबीजाणुक विकास उस प्रक्रिया को दर्शाता है जिसमें तीन गुरुबीजाणुओं के नष्ट होने के बाद केवल एक कार्यशील गुरुबीजाणु से भ्रूणकोष बनता है।

कथन V: आवृतबीजी पादपों में एक प्रारूपिक परिपक्व मादा युग्मकोद्भिद् (भ्रूणकोष) 8-केंद्रकीय और 7-कोशिकीय होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding the funicle and hilum
The stalk attaching the ovule to the placenta is the funicle, and the junctional scar where the body of the ovule attaches to this stalk is the hilum. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding integument encirclement
Although integuments envelop the nutritious nucellus almost entirely, they deliberately leave a narrow pore-like aperture at the apex termed the micropyle, which permits subsequent entry of the pollen tube. Therefore, asserting that integuments leave no opening is scientifically inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding megaspore mother cell meiosis
A single prominent diploid megaspore mother cell (MMC) distinguishes itself within the micropylar hypodermis of the nucellus and completes meiosis to generate four haploid megaspores. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding monosporic development
In standard Polygonum-type ontogeny, three micropylar megaspores disintegrate, leaving the solitary chalazal megaspore to undergo endopolyploid-like nuclear mitotic cycles to build the gametophyte (monosporic development). This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding the 7-celled, 8-nucleate mature embryo sac
Cellularization following the 8-nucleate syncytium produces a three-celled egg apparatus, three chalazal antipodals, and one binucleate central cell, creating a 7-celled, 8-nucleate functional female gametophyte. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Conclusion:
The claims concerning funicle/hilum morphology, MMC meiosis, monosporic ontogeny, and the 7-celled/8-nucleate organization are valid, whereas the claim that integuments leave no opening is invalid. Thus, the first, third, fourth, and fifth claims are correct while the second claim is incorrect.

चरण 1: बीजांडवृंत और नाभिका का मूल्यांकन
बीजांड को अपरा से जोड़ने वाला वृंत बीजांडवृंत कहलाता है तथा बीजांड और बीजांडवृंत का संलयन स्थल नाभिका कहलाता है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 2: अध्यावरण और बीजांडद्वार का मूल्यांकन
अध्यावरण बीजांडकाय को घेरते हैं, परंतु शीर्ष पर एक छोटा छिद्र खुला छोड़ते हैं जिसे बीजांडद्वार (माइक्रोपाइल) कहते हैं। अतः कोई छिद्र न होने का दावा असत्य है।

चरण 3: गुरुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिका के अर्धसूत्री विभाजन का मूल्यांकन
बीजांडकाय के बीजांडद्वारीय सिरे पर एक एकल गुरुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिका विभेदित होकर अर्धसूत्री विभाजन द्वारा चार अगुणित गुरुबीजाणु बनाती है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 4: एकबीजाणुक विकास का मूल्यांकन
चार गुरुबीजाणुओं में से तीन के अपभ्रष्ट होने पर केवल एक कार्यशील गुरुबीजाणु से भ्रूणकोष बनने की प्रक्रिया एकबीजाणुक विकास कहलाती है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 5: परिपक्व भ्रूणकोष की संरचना का मूल्यांकन
परिपक्व आवृतबीजी भ्रूणकोष 7-कोशिकीय और 8-केंद्रकीय होता है (3 अंड उपकरण कोशिकाएं, 3 प्रतिव्यासांत कोशिकाएं और 1 केंद्रीय कोशिका जिसमें 2 ध्रुवीय केंद्रक होते हैं)। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

निष्कर्ष:
बीजांडवृंत/नाभिका, अर्धसूत्री विभाजन, एकबीजाणुक विकास तथा 7-कोशिकीय संरचना से संबंधित विवरण सही हैं, जबकि अध्यावरण द्वारा कोई छिद्र न छोड़ने का विवरण गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, but Statement V is incorrect
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct, but Statement I is incorrect
All Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q03 - Mechanisms and genetic consequences of pollination types

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding types of pollination in angiosperms:

Statement I: Chasmogamous flowers open at maturity and expose their anthers and stigma to external environmental vectors.

Statement II: Cleistogamous flowers remain permanently closed, assuring complete autogamy and dependable seed-set even in the total absence of pollinators.

Statement III: Cleistogamy offers high evolutionary advantage by promoting outcrossing and producing extensive genetic variations in the progeny.

Statement IV: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, but genetically it is similar to autogamy because pollen grains come from the same plant.

Statement V: Xenogamy is the only mode of pollination that introduces genetically distinct pollen grains to the receptive stigma.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे आवृतबीजी पादपों में परागण के प्रकारों के संबंध में पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: उन्मील (चेस्मोगैमस) परागणी पुष्प परिपक्वता पर खुलते हैं तथा अपने परागकोश और वर्तिकाग्र को बाह्य कारकों के लिए अनावृत करते हैं।

कथन II: अनुन्मील्य (क्लिस्टोगैमस) पुष्प हमेशा बंद रहते हैं, जो परागणकों की पूर्ण अनुपस्थिति में भी पूर्ण स्वयुग्मन और सुनिश्चित बीज निर्माण को संभव बनाते हैं।

कथन III: अनुन्मील्य परागण पर-परागण को बढ़ावा देकर तथा संतति में व्यापक आनुवंशिक विभिन्नताएं उत्पन्न करके उच्च विकासवादी लाभ प्रदान करता है।

कथन IV: सजातपुष्पी परागण (गिटोनोगैमी) कार्यात्मक रूप से पर-परागण है जिसमें कारक शामिल होता है, परंतु आनुवंशिक रूप से यह स्वयुग्मन के समान है क्योंकि परागकण उसी पौधे से आते हैं।

कथन V: पर-निषेचन (जीनोगैमी) परागण का एकमात्र ऐसा प्रकार है जो वर्तिकाग्र पर आनुवंशिक रूप से भिन्न प्रकार के परागकण लाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding chasmogamous flowers
Chasmogamous flowers undergo anthesis to expose reproductive stamens and carpels to air currents and animal vectors. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding cleistogamous flowers
Cleistogamous flowers (such as those of Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina) remain unopened, shedding pollen directly onto juxtaposed stigmas inside the bud, guaranteeing seed set without requiring pollinators. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding genetic variation from cleistogamy
Because cleistogamy enforces absolute inbreeding without any possibility of outcrossing, it generates zero genetic recombination and leads to inbreeding depression. Therefore, claiming that cleistogamy promotes outcrossing and extensive genetic variation is scientifically inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding geitonogamy
Geitonogamy transfers pollen between different flowers situated on the same individual plant. Because it requires an ecological transfer vector, it is functionally cross-pollination; however, because all flowers on the individual share identical genotypes, it is genetically identical to autogamy. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding xenogamy
Xenogamy transfers pollen between flowers of genetically distinct individual plants of the species, making it the solitary pollination type that conveys novel allele combinations to the stigma. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Conclusion:
The claims regarding chasmogamy, assured cleistogamous seed set, geitonogamy genetics, and xenogamy variation are valid, whereas the claim that cleistogamy promotes outcrossing is invalid. Thus, the first, second, fourth, and fifth claims are correct while the third claim is incorrect.

चरण 1: उन्मील पुष्पों का मूल्यांकन
उन्मील पुष्प खिलकर अपने परागकोश और वर्तिकाग्र को बाह्य परागण कारकों के संपर्क में लाते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 2: अनुन्मील्य पुष्पों में बीज निर्माण का मूल्यांकन
अनुन्मील्य पुष्प कभी नहीं खुलते, जिससे बिना किसी परागणक के भी परागकण वर्तिकाग्र पर गिरते हैं और बीज निर्माण सुनिश्चित होता है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 3: अनुन्मील्य परागण के आनुवंशिक प्रभाव का मूल्यांकन
अनुन्मील्य परागण अनिवार्य रूप से स्व-परागण कराता है, जिससे कोई नई आनुवंशिक विविधता उत्पन्न नहीं होती बल्कि अंतःप्रजनन अवनति होती है। अतः पर-परागण और विभिन्नता को बढ़ावा देने का दावा असत्य है।

चरण 4: सजातपुष्पी परागण (गिटोनोगैमी) की प्रकृति का मूल्यांकन
सजातपुष्पी परागण में उसी पौधे के एक पुष्प से दूसरे पुष्प पर परागकण जाते हैं; अतः कारक की आवश्यकता के कारण यह कार्यात्मक रूप से पर-परागण है, परंतु एक ही जनक पादप होने के कारण आनुवंशिक रूप से स्वयुग्मन के समान है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 5: पर-निषेचन (जीनोगैमी) का मूल्यांकन
पर-निषेचन ही एकमात्र ऐसा परागण है जो वर्तिकाग्र पर आनुवंशिक रूप से भिन्न परागकण लाता है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

निष्कर्ष:
उन्मील पुष्प, अनुन्मील्य पुष्प की निश्चितता, सजातपुष्पी परागण तथा पर-निषेचन से संबंधित विवरण सही हैं, जबकि अनुन्मील्य परागण द्वारा विभिन्नता उत्पन्न करने का विवरण गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III only are correct
Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct, but Statement I is incorrect
Statements I, II, IV, and V are correct, but Statement III is incorrect
All Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q04 - Comparative analysis of abiotic and biotic pollination syndromes

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding abiotic and biotic pollination mechanisms in angiosperms:

Statement I: The vast majority of flowering plants employ biotic (animal) agents for pollination, whereas only a small proportion rely on abiotic agents.

Statement II: Wind-pollinated flowers produce abundant light, non-sticky pollen grains, and feature well-exposed stamens and large, feathery stigmas.

Statement III: Water pollination (hydrophily) is extremely widespread in nature, occurring routinely across more than 50 percent of all dicotyledonous families.

Statement IV: In Vallisneria, pollination occurs on the surface of water via floating pollen, whereas in marine Zostera, pollination occurs submerged inside water.

Statement V: Animal-pollinated flowers typically provide rewards such as nectar and edible pollen grains, and display conspicuous visual or olfactory attractants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे आवृतबीजी पादपों में अजैव और जैव परागण क्रियाविधियों के संबंध में पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अधिकांश पुष्पी पादप परागण के लिए जैव (जंतु) कारकों का उपयोग करते हैं, जबकि केवल एक छोटा अनुपात अजैव कारकों पर निर्भर करता है।

कथन II: वायु-परागित पुष्प प्रचुर मात्रा में हल्के, चिपचिपाहट रहित परागकण उत्पन्न करते हैं, तथा इनमें सुस्पष्ट अनावृत पुंकेसर और बड़े, रोमिल वर्तिकाग्र होते हैं।

कथन III: जल परागण (हाइड्रोफिली) प्रकृति में अत्यंत व्यापक है और सभी द्विबीजपत्री कुलों के 50 प्रतिशत से अधिक में नियमित रूप से पाया जाता है।

कथन IV: वैलिसनेरिया में परागण जल की सतह पर तैरते परागकणों द्वारा होता है, जबकि समुद्री जोस्टेरा में परागण जल के भीतर डूबी हुई अवस्था में होता है।

कथन V: जंतु-परागित पुष्प आमतौर पर मकरंद और खाद्य परागकण जैसे पुरस्कार प्रदान करते हैं, तथा दृश्य अथवा गंध युक्त आकर्षक प्रदर्शित करते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding biotic vs abiotic pollinator prevalence
The predominance of angiosperms relies on animals (primarily insects like bees) to effect pollen transfer, while abiotic strategies (anemophily and hydrophily) represent minor proportions. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding anemophilous adaptations
Wind-dispersed pollen is produced in massive quantities to offset high dispersal wastage, possessing non-sticky aerodynamic surfaces intercepted by broad plumose stigmas. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding hydrophily prevalence
Pollination by water is exceptionally rare among angiosperms, strictly confined to only about 30 genera, and these are overwhelmingly monocotyledons rather than dicotyledons. Therefore, claiming that hydrophily occurs across more than 50 percent of dicotyledonous families is scientifically inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding Vallisneria and Zostera
Vallisneria exhibits surface hydrophily (epihydrophily) where long stalks bring female flowers to the water surface, whereas Zostera exhibits submerged hydrophily (hypohydrophily) where ribbon-like pollen drifts through seawater currents. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding biotic floral rewards
Zoophilous flowers maintain mutualistic fidelity by offering nutritional rewards (nectar, pollen) or oviposition sites, signaled by vivid pigments or scents. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Conclusion:
The claims regarding biotic dominance, wind pollination syndromes, water pollination mechanics in Vallisneria/Zostera, and animal rewards are valid, whereas the claim asserting widespread hydrophily across dicots is invalid. Thus, the first, second, fourth, and fifth claims are correct while the third claim is incorrect.

चरण 1: जैव बनाम अजैव परागण की व्यापकता का मूल्यांकन
अधिकांश पुष्पी पादप परागण हेतु जंतुओं (विशेषकर कीटों) का उपयोग करते हैं, जबकि अजैव कारक बहुत कम पादपों में उपयोग होते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 2: वायु परागण के अनुकूलनों का मूल्यांकन
वायु-परागित पुष्प भारी मात्रा में हल्के, गैर-चिपचिपे परागकण उत्पन्न करते हैं तथा इनमें खुले पुंकेसर और बड़े रोमिल वर्तिकाग्र पाए जाते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 3: जल परागण की व्यापकता का मूल्यांकन
जल परागण अत्यंत दुर्लभ है और यह केवल लगभग 30 वंशों तक सीमित है, जिनमें अधिकांश एकबीजपत्री हैं। अतः 50% से अधिक द्विबीजपत्री कुलों में इसके पाए जाने का दावा असत्य है।

चरण 4: वैलिसनेरिया और जोस्टेरा में परागण का मूल्यांकन
वैलिसनेरिया में परागण जल की सतह पर होता है (अधिशिरोजल परागण), जबकि जोस्टेरा में परागण जल के भीतर डूबी अवस्था में होता है (अधोजल परागण)। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 5: जंतु परागण में पुष्प पुरस्कारों का मूल्यांकन
जंतु-परागित पुष्प परागणकों को मकरंद और परागकण जैसे पुरस्कार प्रदान करते हैं तथा रंग व सुगंध से उन्हें आकर्षित करते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

निष्कर्ष:
जैव कारकों की प्रधानता, वायु परागण लक्षण, वैलिसनेरिया/जोस्टेरा में परागण तथा पुष्प पुरस्कारों से संबंधित विवरण सही हैं, जबकि द्विबीजपत्रियों में व्यापक जल परागण का विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q05 - Outbreeding contrivances inbreeding depression and pollen pistil dialogue

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding outbreeding devices and pollen-pistil interaction in flowering plants:

Statement I: Continuous self-pollination in hermaphrodite flowers results in inbreeding depression.

Statement II: Spatial separation of anthers and stigma (herkogamy) prevents autogamy in bisexual flowers.

Statement III: Self-incompatibility is a genetically controlled mechanism that inhibits self-pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the style.

Statement IV: In monoecious plants such as castor and maize, both autogamy and geitonogamy are completely prevented.

Statement V: The acceptance or rejection of pollen by the pistil is mediated by a continuous dynamic chemical dialogue between pollen and pistil tissues.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे पुष्पी पादपों में बहिःप्रजनन युक्तियों तथा पराग-स्त्रीकेसर पारस्परिक क्रिया के संबंध में पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: द्विलिंगी पुष्पों में निरंतर स्व-परागण के परिणामस्वरूप अंतःप्रजनन अवनति होती है।

कथन II: परागकोश और वर्तिकाग्र को अलग-अलग स्थितियों पर रखना द्विलिंगी पुष्पों में स्वयुग्मन (ऑटोगैमी) को रोकता है।

कथन III: स्व-असामंजस्य एक आनुवंशिक रूप से नियंत्रित क्रियाविधि है जो वर्तिका में स्व-पराग के अंकुरण अथवा पराग नली की वृद्धि को रोकती है।

कथन IV: अरंडी और मक्का जैसे उभयलिंगाश्रयी (मोनोएशियस) पादपों में, स्वयुग्मन और सजातपुष्पी परागण दोनों पूरी तरह रुक जाते हैं।

कथन V: स्त्रीकेसर द्वारा पराग की स्वीकृति अथवा अस्वीकृति पराग और स्त्रीकेसर के ऊतकों के बीच एक सतत गतिशील रासायनिक संवाद द्वारा मध्यस्थ होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding inbreeding depression
Obligate self-fertilisation across generations exposes deleterious recessive alleles, steadily reducing vigor, fecundity, and environmental adaptability (inbreeding depression). This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding spatial separation (herkogamy)
Positioning anthers and receptive stigmas at different physical heights or orientations mechanically hinders the transfer of self-pollen within the same blossom, averting autogamy. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding self-incompatibility
Self-incompatibility operates as an active biochemical checkpoint governed by genetic alleles that arrests pollen germination on the stigma surface or arrests pollen tube elongation within stylistic transmitting tissue. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding monoecious plants
Monoecy separates staminate and pistillate flowers on the same individual plant. While this successfully avoids autogamy, it does not impede geitonogamy because pollen from male flowers can readily reach female flowers on the identical parent. Complete prevention of both autogamy and geitonogamy necessitates dioecy (as seen in papaya). Therefore, claiming that monoecy prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy is scientifically inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding the chemical dialogue
Pollen-pistil interaction is orchestrated through reciprocal molecular signaling involving pollen wall proteins, stylar glycoproteins, and signal transduction cascades that culminate in physiological acceptance or active rejection. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Conclusion:
The claims regarding inbreeding depression, spatial separation, self-incompatibility, and chemical recognition dialogue are valid, whereas the claim that monoecy prevents geitonogamy is invalid. Thus, the first, second, third, and fifth claims are correct while the fourth claim is incorrect.

चरण 1: अंतःप्रजनन अवनति का मूल्यांकन
द्विलिंगी पुष्पों में लगातार स्व-परागण होने से पादप की जीवनक्षमता और उत्पादकता में कमी आती है जिसे अंतःप्रजनन अवनति कहते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 2: परागकोश और वर्तिकाग्र की स्थिति का मूल्यांकन
परागकोश और वर्तिकाग्र को अलग-अलग स्तरों पर रखने से परागकण उसी पुष्प के वर्तिकाग्र तक नहीं पहुंच पाते, जिससे स्वयुग्मन रुकता है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 3: स्व-असामंजस्य की क्रियाविधि का मूल्यांकन
स्व-असामंजस्य एक आनुवंशिक क्रियाविधि है जो वर्तिकाग्र या वर्तिका में अपने ही पराग के अंकुरण अथवा नली की वृद्धि को रोकती है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 4: उभयलिंगाश्रयी पादपों में परागण का मूल्यांकन
उभयलिंगाश्रयी पादप (जैसे मक्का और अरंडी) में नर और मादा पुष्प एक ही पौधे पर होते हैं। यह व्यवस्था स्वयुग्मन को तो रोकती है, परंतु सजातपुष्पी परागण को नहीं रोक पाती। दोनों को रोकने के लिए एकलिंगाश्रयी होना आवश्यक है। अतः यह दावा असत्य है।

चरण 5: रासायनिक संवाद का मूल्यांकन
परागकण और स्त्रीकेसर के बीच निरंतर रासायनिक घटकों के आदान-प्रदान और संवाद से ही पराग की पहचान, स्वीकृति या अस्वीकृति होती है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

निष्कर्ष:
अंतःप्रजनन अवनति, स्थानिक पृथक्करण, स्व-असामंजस्य तथा रासायनिक संवाद से संबंधित विवरण सही हैं, जबकि उभयलिंगाश्रयी पादपों द्वारा सजातपुष्पी परागण रोकने का विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q06 - Endosperm consumption perisperm monocot embryo and apomictic polyembryony

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding post-fertilisation events, seed structure, and apomixis in angiosperms:

Statement I: Endosperm development precedes embryo development as an adaptation to provide assured nutrition to the dividing zygote and proembryo.

Statement II: In non-albuminous seeds such as pea and groundnut, the endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo prior to seed maturation.

Statement III: Residual, persistent nucellus retained in the mature seeds of black pepper and beet is known as perisperm.

Statement IV: In monocotyledonous grass embryos, the solitary shield-shaped cotyledon attached laterally to the embryonal axis is called the scutellum.

Statement V: In polyembryonic varieties of Citrus and mango, multiple embryos arise exclusively because the diploid zygote undergoes repeated meiotic divisions inside the embryo sac.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे आवृतबीजी पादपों में निषेचनोत्तर घटनाओं, बीज संरचना तथा असंगजनन के संबंध में पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: विकासशील युग्मनज और प्राक्भ्रूण को सुनिश्चित पोषण प्रदान करने के अनुकूलन के रूप में भ्रूणपोष का विकास भ्रूण विकास से पहले होता है।

कथन II: गैर-एल्ब्यूमिनस (अभ्रूणपोषी) बीजों जैसे मटर और मूंगफली में, बीज परिपक्व होने से पूर्व भ्रूणपोष विकासशील भ्रूण द्वारा पूरी तरह से उपभोग कर लिया जाता है।

कथन III: काली मिर्च और चुकंदर के परिपक्व बीजों में शेष बचा हुआ, स्थायी बीजांडकाय परिभ्रूणपोष (पेरिस्पर्म) कहलाता है।

कथन IV: एकबीजपत्री घास के भ्रूण में, भ्रूणीय अक्ष के पार्श्व में जुड़ा एकल ढालनुमा बीजपत्र प्रशल्क (स्कुटेलम) कहलाता है।

कथन V: सिट्रस और आम की बहुभ्रूणीय किस्मों में, अनेक भ्रूण केवल इसलिए बनते हैं क्योंकि द्विगुणित युग्मनज भ्रूणकोष के भीतर बार-बार अर्धसूत्री विभाजन करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding endosperm developmental precedence
The primary endosperm cell initiates mitotic proliferation prior to zygotic division to establish an abundant nutrient reservoir, ensuring that the embryonic lineage receives adequate sustenance. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding non-albuminous seeds
In exalbuminous seeds such as legumes (pea, groundnut, beans), the endosperm tissue is completely digested and absorbed into swollen storage cotyledons before the seed enters desiccation. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding perisperm in black pepper and beet
Whereas nucellar tissue normally vanishes during seed ontogeny, persistent diploid vegetative nucellar remnants endure as perisperm in taxa like Piper nigrum and Beta vulgaris. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding the grass scutellum
In Poaceae (grasses), the solitary cotyledon is modified into an expanded, absorptive shield situated along one side of the embryonal axis and is termed the scutellum. This claim is scientifically accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding polyembryony in Citrus and mango
In apomictic polyembryonic Citrus and mango varieties, additional embryos originate when maternal diploid somatic nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide mitotically, push into the embryo sac lumen, and mature into embryos. Zygotes never undergo meiosis to produce embryos. Therefore, claiming that zygotes divide meiotically to yield multiple embryos is scientifically inaccurate.

Conclusion:
The claims regarding endosperm precedence, non-albuminous seed storage, perisperm identity, and scutellum anatomy are valid, whereas the claim attributing polyembryony to zygotic meiosis is invalid. Thus, the first, second, third, and fourth claims are correct while the fifth claim is incorrect.

चरण 1: भ्रूणपोष विकास के पूर्वागमन का मूल्यांकन
विकासशील भ्रूण को सुनिश्चित पोषण प्रदान करने के लिए प्राथमिक भ्रूणपोष कोशिका युग्मनज से पहले विभाजित होकर भ्रूणपोष ऊतक बनाती है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 2: अभ्रूणपोषी (गैर-एल्ब्यूमिनस) बीजों का मूल्यांकन
मटर और मूंगफली जैसे बीजों में बीज के परिपक्व होने से पहले भ्रूणपोष पूरी तरह समाप्त हो जाता है और भोजन बीजपत्रों में संचित होता है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 3: परिभ्रूणपोष (पेरिस्पर्म) का मूल्यांकन
काली मिर्च और चुकंदर में अवशिष्ट, स्थायी बीजांडकाय बीज में बना रहता है, जिसे परिभ्रूणपोष कहते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 4: घास के प्रशल्क (स्कुटेलम) का मूल्यांकन
घास कुल के भ्रूण में एकल बीजपत्र ढाल के आकार का होता है जो पार्श्व में स्थित होता है और प्रशल्क कहलाता है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 5: सिट्रस और आम में बहुभ्रूणता का मूल्यांकन
सिट्रस और आम में अतिरिक्त भ्रूण बीजांडकाय की द्विगुणित कायिक कोशिकाओं के समसूत्री विभाजन और भ्रूणकोष में प्रवर्धन से बनते हैं। युग्मनज में अर्धसूत्री विभाजन से भ्रूण नहीं बनते। अतः यह दावा असत्य है।

निष्कर्ष:
भ्रूणपोष के विकास क्रम, अभ्रूणपोषी बीजों, परिभ्रूणपोष तथा प्रशल्क से संबंधित विवरण सही हैं, जबकि युग्मनज में अर्धसूत्री विभाजन से बहुभ्रूणता का विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Functional roles of anther wall layers

questiontext.text:
Match the microsporangial wall layers in List-I with their corresponding functions or characteristics in List-II:

List-I (Wall Layer) List-II (Function / Characteristic)
A. Tapetum I. Protection and dehiscence of anther
B. Endothecium II. Nourishes developing microspores and possesses dense cytoplasm
C. Middle layers III. Outermost single protective cellular envelope
D. Epidermis IV. Ephemeral wall layers situated between endothecium and tapetum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the structure and function of the tapetum.
The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium. Its cells possess dense cytoplasm, are frequently multinucleate, and function primarily to nourish developing pollen grains. Thus, A corresponds to II.

Step 2: Analyze the role of the endothecium.
The endothecium lies immediately interior to the epidermis. Along with the outer layers, it provides structural protection and develops fibrous thickenings that assist in the dehiscence of the mature anther to liberate pollen. Thus, B corresponds to I.

Step 3: Analyze the middle layers.
The middle layers comprise one to three cellular tiers positioned between the endothecium and tapetum. These are short-lived (ephemeral) layers that degenerate as pollen matures. Thus, C corresponds to IV.

Step 4: Analyze the epidermis.
The epidermis forms the outermost continuous protective bounding layer around the entire anther. Thus, D corresponds to III.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
Combining all specific structural associations: Tapetum pairs with nourishing developing microspores (A-II), Endothecium pairs with protection and dehiscence (B-I), Middle layers pair with ephemeral intermediate tiers (C-IV), and Epidermis pairs with the outermost protective layer (D-III). The correct matching arrangement is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

answer.text: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Structural components of the angiosperm ovule

questiontext.text:
Match the anatomical regions of an angiosperm ovule in List-I with their accurate anatomical descriptions in List-II:

List-I (Ovule Structure) List-II (Description)
A. Funicle I. Basal region of the ovule opposite the micropyle
B. Hilum II. Small pore through which oxygen and water enter during germination
C. Integument III. Stalk by which an ovule is attached to the placenta
D. Chalaza IV. Junction where the body of the ovule fuses with its stalk

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the funicle.
The funicle is the stalk attaching the megasporangium (ovule) directly to the maternal placenta within the ovarian cavity. Thus, A corresponds to III.

Step 2: Evaluate the hilum.
The hilum represents the precise scar or region where the main body of the ovule fuses with the funicle. Thus, B corresponds to IV.

Step 3: Evaluate the micropyle and integuments.
While the micropyle is the small pore remaining at the apex that facilitates moisture and gas entry, protective envelopes surrounding the nucellus are integuments. In this context, chalaza represents the basal region opposite the micropyle. Thus, D corresponds to I.

Step 4: Relate remaining structural descriptions.
Matching each anatomical landmark systematically gives: Funicle attaches ovule to placenta (III), Hilum represents the junction of ovule and funicle (IV), Micropylar opening facilitates entry of oxygen and water (II), and Chalaza represents the basal region of the ovule (I). Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
The correct matching combination is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Pollen grain structural features and cellular components

questiontext.text:
Match the pollen grain components in List-I with their characteristic features in List-II:

List-I (Pollen Component) List-II (Feature / Property)
A. Exine I. Thin, continuous internal layer composed of cellulose and pectin
B. Intine II. Small, spindle-shaped cell with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus
C. Vegetative cell III. Highly resistant outer coat composed of sporopollenin
D. Generative cell IV. Larger cell containing abundant food reserve and an irregular nucleus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Detail the characteristics of the exine.
The exine is the outer sculptured wall layer made of sporopollenin, an extraordinarily resistant organic substance capable of withstanding extreme temperatures, strong acids, and alkalis. Thus, A corresponds to III.

Step 2: Detail the characteristics of the intine.
The intine is the inner wall layer of the pollen grain; it is thin, continuous, and chemically constituted of cellulose and pectin. Thus, B corresponds to I.

Step 3: Detail the vegetative cell.
During pollen differentiation, unequal division produces a vegetative cell that is larger in volume, contains abundant nutrient reserves, and has a large, irregularly shaped nucleus. Thus, C corresponds to IV.

Step 4: Detail the generative cell.
The generative cell is small, spindle-shaped, contains dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, and floats freely within the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell. Thus, D corresponds to II.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
The established pairings are Exine with sporopollenin layer (A-III), Intine with continuous cellulose-pectin layer (B-I), Vegetative cell with large nutrient-rich cell (C-IV), and Generative cell with small spindle-shaped cell (D-II). The correct matching combination is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Cells of the mature female gametophyte

questiontext.text:
Match the cellular entities of a mature 7-celled, 8-nucleate embryo sac in List-I with their correct characteristics or functions in List-II:

List-I (Embryo Sac Component) List-II (Characteristic / Function)
A. Synergids I. Three cells situated at the chalazal end
B. Antipodals II. Possess filiform apparatus at micropylar tip to guide pollen tube
C. Central cell III. Haploid female gamete that undergoes syngamy
D. Egg cell IV. Largest binucleate cell containing two polar nuclei

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characterize the synergids.
Synergids are paired cells flanking the egg cell at the micropylar end; they exhibit special micropylar cellular finger-like thickenings called the filiform apparatus, which play an essential role in directing pollen tube entry. Thus, A corresponds to II.

Step 2: Characterize the antipodal cells.
Antipodals are a group of three cells organized at the chalazal pole of the female gametophyte. Thus, B corresponds to I.

Step 3: Characterize the central cell.
The central cell is the voluminous central entity of the embryo sac containing two haploid polar nuclei situated beneath the egg apparatus. Thus, C corresponds to IV.

Step 4: Characterize the egg cell.
The egg cell represents the single haploid functional female gamete positioned at the micropylar end that fuses with a male gamete during syngamy to generate the diploid zygote. Thus, D corresponds to III.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
The accurate pairings are Synergids with filiform apparatus (A-II), Antipodals with chalazal cells (B-I), Central cell with binucleate large cell (C-IV), and Egg cell with female gamete (D-III). The correct matching combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Pollination adaptations and representative plant examples

questiontext.text:
Match the plants in List-I with their respective pollination mechanisms or floral adaptations in List-II:

List-I (Plant) List-II (Pollination Feature)
A. Vallisneria I. Cleistogamous flowers ensuring autogamy without pollinators
B. Zostera II. Female flowers reach water surface via long stalks to meet floating pollen
C. Viola III. Submerged marine seagrass with long, ribbon-like pollen grains
D. Maize IV. Wind-pollinated with well-exposed stamens and feathery stigmas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze pollination in Vallisneria.
In the freshwater plant Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the water surface by an uncoiling long stalk, where passive water currents carry floating pollen grains to contact the stigma (epihydrophily). Thus, A corresponds to II.

Step 2: Analyze pollination in Zostera.
In marine sea-grasses like Zostera, flowers remain entirely submerged, and long, ribbon-like, mucilage-coated pollen grains are transported passively inside the water column (hypohydrophily). Thus, B corresponds to III.

Step 3: Analyze pollination in Viola.
Viola (common pansy) produces two types of flowers, including cleistogamous flowers that never open, thereby guaranteeing autogamy and seed set even in the complete absence of external pollinators. Thus, C corresponds to I.

Step 4: Analyze pollination in maize (corn).
Grasses such as maize are anemophilous (wind-pollinated); they bear compact inflorescences with versatile, well-exposed stamens and prominent, feathery styles and stigmas that wave in the wind to trap air-borne pollen. Thus, D corresponds to IV.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
The specific associations are Vallisneria with surface water pollination (A-II), Zostera with submerged ribbon-like pollen (B-III), Viola with cleistogamous flowers (C-I), and Maize with wind pollination (D-IV). The correct matching combination is A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Outbreeding mechanisms preventing inbreeding depression

questiontext.text:
Match the outbreeding devices listed in List-I with their corresponding definitions or functional outcomes in List-II:

List-I (Outbreeding Mechanism) List-II (Mechanism / Consequence)
A. Dichogamy I. Genetic mechanism inhibiting self-pollen germination or tube growth
B. Heterostyly / Spatial separation II. Presence of male and female flowers on different plants, preventing both autogamy and geitonogamy
C. Self-incompatibility III. Non-synchronous timing of pollen release and stigma receptivity
D. Dioecy IV. Anther and stigma placed at different positions preventing contact

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine dichogamy.
Dichogamy is the temporal separation of reproductive organ maturation, wherein pollen shedding and stigma receptivity are not synchronised, thereby preventing autogamy. Thus, A corresponds to III.

Step 2: Examine spatial separation (herkogamy/heterostyly).
Placing anther and stigma at different spatial levels ensures that pollen cannot directly contact the stigma of the same flower. Thus, B corresponds to IV.

Step 3: Examine self-incompatibility.
Self-incompatibility is a genetically controlled physiological barrier preventing self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers on the same plant) from fertilising ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube extension in the style. Thus, C corresponds to I.

Step 4: Examine dioecy.
Dioecy occurs when individual plants bear strictly unisexual (male or female) flowers (e.g., papaya). Because individuals are separate sexes, this condition entirely prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. Thus, D corresponds to II.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
The correct pairings are Dichogamy with non-synchronous maturation (A-III), Spatial placement with physical separation of anther and stigma (B-IV), Self-incompatibility with genetic inhibition of self-pollen (C-I), and Dioecy with prevention of both autogamy and geitonogamy (D-II). The correct matching combination is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

answer.text: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Post-fertilisation structures and embryological terms

questiontext.text:
Match the post-fertilisation embryonic structures in List-I with their botanical definitions in List-II:

List-I (Embryonic Structure) List-II (Definition / Feature)
A. Scutellum I. Residual, persistent nucellus in mature seeds
B. Coleoptile II. Single shield-shaped lateral cotyledon in grass family
C. Coleorrhiza III. Hollow foliar sheath enclosing shoot apex and leaf primordia
D. Perisperm IV. Undifferentiated protective sheath enclosing radicle and root cap

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify scutellum.
In monocotyledonous embryos, particularly of the grass family, the single cotyledon is large, shield-shaped, and situated laterally relative to the embryonal axis; it is termed the scutellum. Thus, A corresponds to II.

Step 2: Identify coleoptile.
Above the attachment point of the scutellum, the epicotyl contains the shoot apex and leaf primordia enclosed within a protective hollow foliar sheath called the coleoptile. Thus, B corresponds to III.

Step 3: Identify coleorrhiza.
At the lower end of the monocot embryonal axis, the radicle and root cap are covered by an undifferentiated protective sheath termed the coleorrhiza. Thus, C corresponds to IV.

Step 4: Identify perisperm.
In certain seeds like black pepper and beet, remnants of the maternal nutritive tissue (nucellus) persist outside the embryo and endosperm; this residual persistent nucellus is called perisperm. Thus, D corresponds to I.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
The correct pairs are Scutellum with single shield-shaped cotyledon (A-II), Coleoptile with foliar sheath covering shoot apex (B-III), Coleorrhiza with sheath covering radicle (C-IV), and Perisperm with persistent nucellus (D-I). The correct matching combination is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questiontext.text:

List-I (Entity) List-II (Biological Fact)
A. Lupinus arcticus I. Tallest flower (about 6 feet) offering safe site for insect egg-laying

Seeds of Lupinus arcticus excavated from the Arctic Tundra hold the record for dormancy, having successfully germinated and flowered after an estimated 10,000 years. Thus, A corresponds to II.

Step 2: Evaluate Phoenix dactylifera.
A 2,000-year-old viable date palm seed (Phoenix dactylifera) was recovered during archaeological excavations at King Herod's palace near the Dead Sea. Thus, B corresponds to III.

Step 3: Evaluate Parthenium.
Parthenium (carrot grass) was inadvertently introduced into India as a contaminant with imported wheat and has become a ubiquitous weed whose airborne pollen triggers severe respiratory allergies and asthma. Thus, C corresponds to IV.

Step 4: Evaluate Amorphophallus.
The flower of Amorphophallus is colossal (approximately 6 feet high) and provides floral rewards by offering a safe oviposition (egg-laying) shelter for its insect visitors. Thus, D corresponds to I.

The correlations are Lupinus arcticus with 10,000-year seed dormancy (A-II), Phoenix dactylifera with 2,000-year-old viable seed (B-III), Parthenium with allergen contaminant (C-IV), and Amorphophallus with 6-foot flower oviposition reward (D-I). name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Types of fruits and reproductive conditions with examples

questiontext.text:
Match the reproductive conditions or fruit types in List-I with their characteristic plant examples in List-II:

List-I (Condition / Fruit Type) List-II (Plant Example)
A. False fruit I. Banana
B. Parthenocarpic fruit II. Apple

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate false fruit.
In false fruits (pseudocarps), floral parts other than the ovary contribute significantly to fruit formation; in apple, strawberry, and cashew, the fleshy edible part is derived largely from the thalamus. Thus, A corresponds to II.

Step 2: Evaluate parthenocarpic fruit.
Parthenocarpic fruits develop without fertilisation and are naturally seedless; banana is a classic textbook example. Thus, B corresponds to I.

Step 3: Evaluate apomixis via nucellar polyembryony.
In many varieties of Citrus and mango, maternal diploid nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide actively, push into the embryo sac, and develop into multiple embryos (polyembryony). Thus, C corresponds to IV.

Step 4: Evaluate albuminous dicot seed.
While most dicot seeds (e.g., pea, groundnut, beans) are non-albuminous (exalbuminous), castor is a prominent dicotyledonous seed that retains a persistent, nutrient-rich endosperm at maturity (albuminous). Thus, D corresponds to III.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
Connecting each term to its representative plant: False fruit pairs with Apple (A-II), Parthenocarpic fruit pairs with Banana (B-I), Maternal nucellar polyembryony pairs with Citrus (C-IV), and Albuminous dicot seed pairs with Castor (D-III). The correct matching combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Double fertilisation events and ploidy of tissues

questiontext.text:
Match the embryological events or structures in List-I with their accurate biological descriptions and ploidy states in List-II:

List-I (Event / Structure) List-II (Biological Description and Ploidy)
A. Syngamy I. Triploid tissue originating from triple fusion that provides nourishment
B. Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) II. Diploid cell formed by the fusion of one haploid male gamete with the haploid egg nucleus
C. Endosperm III. Product of fusion of a haploid male gamete with two haploid polar nuclei (\(3n\))
D. Zygote IV. Fusion of a male gamete with female gamete generating the diploid progenitor of the embryo

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define syngamy.
Syngamy is the generative fusion of one haploid sperm nucleus with the haploid egg nucleus, resulting in the diploid zygote. Thus, A corresponds to IV.

Step 2: Define Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN).
The second male gamete moves to the central cell and fuses with the two polar nuclei, undergoing triple fusion to establish the triploid (\(3n\)) Primary Endosperm Nucleus. Thus, B corresponds to III.

Step 3: Define endosperm.
The Primary Endosperm Cell undergoes repeated mitotic divisions to form the triploid nutritive endosperm tissue, which stores food reserves for the developing embryo. Thus, C corresponds to I.

Step 4: Define zygote.
The zygote is the single-celled diploid (\(2n\)) product resulting directly from syngamy, which subsequently undergoes embryogeny to produce the embryo. Thus, D corresponds to II.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
Pairing each concept: Syngamy is generative fertilisation producing the diploid progenitor (A-IV), Primary Endosperm Nucleus is the triploid product of triple fusion (B-III), Endosperm is the triploid nutritive tissue (C-I), and Zygote is the diploid product of male and egg gamete fusion (D-II). The correct matching combination is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_SEQUENCING_MCQ_Q01 - Developmental sequence of microsporogenesis to male gamete formation

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following stages and structures in the correct chronological sequence of microgametogenesis and pollen development within an angiosperm anther:

  1. Differentiation of potential pollen mother cells (PMCs) from homogenous cells
  2. Meiotic reduction division resulting in a cluster of four cells (microspore tetrad)
  3. Compactly arranged homogenous sporogenous tissue occupying the centre of the young microsporangium
  4. Dehydration and maturation of microspores dissociating into functional pollen grains
  5. Mitotic division of the generative cell yielding two functional male gametes

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the initial embryonic tissue in the microsporangium.
In a young anther, the centre of each microsporangium is initially occupied by a compact group of homogenous diploid cells known as the sporogenous tissue. Thus, stage III represents the starting point.

Step 2: Trace differentiation into pollen mother cells.
As the anther develops further, each diploid cell of the sporogenous tissue acts as a potential microspore mother cell or pollen mother cell (PMC). Thus, stage I follows stage III.

Step 3: Account for microsporogenesis.
Each pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis (microsporogenesis) to form a cluster of four haploid cells arranged as a microspore tetrad. Thus, stage II follows stage I.

Step 4: Trace pollen grain formation.
As the anther matures and dehydrates, the microspores dissociate from one another and develop specialized outer exine and inner intine walls to become independent pollen grains. Thus, stage IV follows stage II.

Step 5: Account for male gamete generation and conclude.
Finally, the generative cell of the pollen grain divides mitotically—either before shedding (at the 3-celled stage) or during pollen tube growth—to produce two non-motile male gametes. Thus, stage V represents the terminal step.
The correct chronological order of stages is: III → I → II → IV → V.

answer.text: I → III → II → IV → V
III → I → II → IV → V
III → II → I → IV → V
I → II → III → IV → V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_SEQUENCING_MCQ_Q02 - Chronological sequence of pollen pistil interaction and fertilisation events

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following physiological and cellular events of pollen-pistil interaction and double fertilisation in their correct chronological sequence:

  1. Growth of the pollen tube through the intercellular spaces of the style towards the ovary
  2. Entry of the pollen tube into one of the synergids directed by the filiform apparatus
  3. Germination of a compatible pollen grain on the receptive stigma through a germ pore
  4. Discharge of two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the receptive synergid
  5. Simultaneous occurrences of syngamy and triple fusion within the embryo sac
  6. Entry of the pollen tube into the ovule through the micropylar aperture

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Initiation of germination following compatible recognition.
Upon successful chemical recognition and acceptance of a compatible pollen grain on the stigma, the pollen grain hydrates and germinates to produce a pollen tube through one of its germ pores. Thus, step III is the initial event.

Step 2: Traversal through stylar tissues.
The vegetative nucleus and generative contents enter the emerging tube, and the pollen tube grows chemotropically through the transmitting tissues of the stigma and style to reach the ovary. Thus, step I follows step III.

Step 3: Entry into the megasporangium (ovule).
After reaching the ovarian cavity, the pollen tube approaches the ovule and enters it through the micropyle. Thus, step VI follows step I.

Step 4: Penetration into the female gametophyte.
At the micropylar end of the embryo sac, special cellular thickenings called the filiform apparatus guide the entry of the pollen tube into the cytoplasm of one of the synergids. Thus, step II follows step VI.

Step 5: Discharge of male gametes.
The tip of the pollen tube ruptures within the penetrated synergid, releasing both male gametes into the synergid cytoplasm. Thus, step IV follows step II.

Step 6: Completion of double fertilisation.
One male gamete moves to the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus (syngamy), while the second male gamete moves to the central cell and fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion), completing the process of double fertilisation. Thus, step V is the concluding event.
The complete chronological sequence is: III → I → VI → II → IV → V.

answer.text: III → I → II → VI → IV → V
I → III → VI → II → IV → V
III → I → VI → II → IV → V
III → VI → I → II → IV → V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Primary function of tapetum layer

questiontext.text: In the transverse section of a typical young angiosperm anther, which of the following wall layers is the innermost and directly functions in nourishing the developing pollen grains?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A typical microsporangium is surrounded by four distinct wall layers: the outer epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, and the innermost tapetum.

Step 2: Functional Role Analysis
The outer three layers (epidermis, endothecium, and middle layers) provide mechanical protection and assist in anther dehiscence to release pollen. In contrast, the innermost layer, the tapetum, possesses dense cytoplasm, frequently becomes multinucleate, and supplies vital nutrients to the developing microspores.

Final Answer:
The innermost wall layer that nourishes developing pollen grains is the tapetum.

answer.text: Tapetum
Endothecium
Epidermis
Middle layers

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Chemical nature of pollen exine

questiontext.text: The hard outer protective layer of an angiosperm pollen grain, the exine, is composed of which highly resistant organic substance?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The pollen grain wall exhibits a two-layered architecture comprising an outer exine and an inner intine.

Step 2: Material Properties
The exine is composed of sporopollenin, recognized as one of the most resistant organic biomaterials known. Sporopollenin withstands high temperatures, strong acids, and alkali, and no enzyme capable of degrading it has been identified. By comparison, the intine is a thin continuous layer made of cellulose and pectin.

Final Answer:
The substance constituting the exine is sporopollenin.

answer.text: Cellulose and pectin

Hemicellulose

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Pollen shedding stage in majority of angiosperms

questiontext.text: In more than 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed from the anthers at which developmental stage?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During pollen maturation, asymmetric spindle division divides the microspore into a larger vegetative cell and a smaller generative cell.

Step 2: Angiosperm Frequency
In over 60 percent of flowering plants, pollen grains are released at this 2-celled stage consisting of one vegetative cell and one generative cell. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically prior to shedding to form two male gametes, shedding at the 3-celled stage.

Final Answer:
In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage.

answer.text: 1-celled stage

Pollen grains of certain invasive anemophilous weeds can induce respiratory afflictions such as asthma and bronchitis in humans.

Step 2: Specific Occurrence
Parthenium hysterophorus (commonly known as carrot grass) entered India inadvertently as an adulterant in imported wheat shipments. It rapidly naturalized across India and is widely recognized as a major aeroallergen.

Final Answer:
The allergen-causing contaminant weed is Parthenium (carrot grass).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Cellular and nuclear organisation of mature embryo sac

questiontext.text: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac (female gametophyte) exhibits which structural organisation of cells and nuclei?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Female gametophyte ontogeny proceeds through free-nuclear divisions of the functional megaspore followed by cellular compartmentalization.

Step 2: Structural Breakdown
Three free-nuclear mitotic divisions produce 8 nuclei. Wall formation encloses 6 nuclei into individual cells: three at the micropylar pole forming the egg apparatus (two synergids and one egg cell) and three at the chalazal pole forming antipodal cells. The remaining two polar nuclei remain within the large central cell. Consequently, the mature female gametophyte is 7-celled and 8-nucleate.

Final Answer:
The mature embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate.

questiontext.text: The filiform apparatus is a specialized cellular thickening present at the micropylar tip of which cells in the embryo sac?

Step 2: Structural and Functional Localization
Special finger-like cellular wall thickenings called the filiform apparatus are located at the micropylar tip of the synergids. These thickenings play a crucial role in directing and guiding the entry of the pollen tube into the synergid.

Final Answer:

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q08 - Characteristic feature of cleistogamous flowers

questiontext.text: Which of the following is an invariant biological characteristic of cleistogamous flowers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Certain plant taxa (such as Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina) produce two types of flowers: chasmogamous (which open and display floral organs) and cleistogamous.

Step 2: Cleistogamy Evaluation
Cleistogamous flowers remain permanently closed throughout their lifecycle. Because their anthers and stigma are enclosed together, dehiscence of anthers in the flower bud results in assured self-pollination (autogamy) and reliable seed-set completely independent of pollinator availability.

Final Answer:
Cleistogamous flowers never open and ensure autogamous seed-set in the absence of pollinators.

answer.text: They open widely to display vibrant petals to attract bee pollinators
They produce copious sweet nectar to sustain vertebrate visitors
They rely exclusively on wind currents for cross-pollination
They do not open at all, ensuring autogamy even without pollinators

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q09 - Dual nuclear fusions defining double fertilisation

questiontext.text: The event of double fertilisation, unique to angiosperms, consists of which two specific fusion processes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A discharged pollen tube releases two haploid male gametes into the cytoplasm of a receptive synergid.

Step 2: Fusion Analysis
One male gamete migrates and fuses with the haploid egg nucleus (syngamy) to form the diploid zygote. Simultaneously, the second male gamete moves to the central cell and fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) to produce the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). Because two distinct fusions occur within the embryo sac, the phenomenon is termed double fertilisation.

Final Answer:
Double fertilisation comprises syngamy and triple fusion.

answer.text: Syngamy and triple fusion
Syngamy and apomixis
Parthenogenesis and triple fusion
Autogamy and geitonogamy

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q10 - Ploidy level of primary endosperm nucleus

questiontext.text: What is the normal ploidy level of the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) formed following double fertilisation in a typical angiosperm?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Triple fusion involves the coalescence of three distinct haploid nuclei inside the central cell.

Step 2: Nuclear Accounting
The central cell contains two haploid polar nuclei (\(n + n\)). The second male gamete is haploid (\(n\)). Their union results in a single nucleus containing \(n + n + n = 3n\) chromosomes, termed the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).

Final Answer:
The ploidy of the primary endosperm nucleus is triploid (\(3n\)).

answer.text: Diploid (\(2n\))
Triploid (\(3n\))
Haploid (\(n\))
Tetraploid (\(4n\))

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q11 - Division type and ploidy during microsporogenesis

questiontext.text: During microsporogenesis, cells of the sporogenous tissue function as pollen mother cells (PMCs). What type of cell division occurs and what is the resulting ploidy of the microspores in the tetrad?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microsporogenesis is the developmental process whereby microspores are formed from sporogenous tissue within the microsporangium.

Step 2: Division and Ploidy Analysis
Each potential pollen mother cell (PMC) is diploid (\(2n\)). To reduce chromosome number and generate gametophytic units, it undergoes meiosis (reduction division) to produce a cluster of four cells known as a microspore tetrad. Each individual microspore in the tetrad is genetically haploid (\(n\)).

Final Answer:
PMCs undergo meiotic division to form haploid (\(n\)) microspores.

answer.text: Mitotic division yielding diploid (\(2n\)) microspores
Free-nuclear division yielding triploid (\(3n\)) microspores
Meiotic division yielding haploid (\(n\)) microspores
Amitotic division yielding polyploid microspores

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q12 - Cytological features of tapetal cells

questiontext.text: Which of the following descriptions accurately characterizes the cytological features of mature tapetal cells in an angiosperm anther?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The tapetum forms the innermost physiological boundary layer lining each pollen sac.

Step 2: Cytological Evaluation
Because of their intense metabolic and secretor activity in nourishing microspores, tapetal cells contain prominent dense cytoplasm and often undergo endomitosis or free nuclear division without cytokinesis, causing them to become bi-nucleate or multinucleate.

Final Answer:
Tapetal cells possess dense cytoplasm and are generally multinucleate.

answer.text: Contain sparse cytoplasm with a single highly condensed haploid nucleus
Possess highly lignified, thick secondary walls lacking cytoplasmic contents
Are highly vacuolated, completely enucleated, and dead at maturity
Possess dense cytoplasm and frequently contain more than one nucleus

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q13 - Distinction between vegetative and generative cells

questiontext.text: In a mature 2-celled angiosperm pollen grain, how does the vegetative cell compare morphologically with the generative cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Unequal mitosis of a microspore yields two structurally and functionally divergent cells within the pollen grain.

Step 2: Morphological Comparison
The vegetative cell is distinctly bigger, loaded with abundant starch and nutrient reserves, and contains a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small, spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, and floats freely within the vegetative cell's cytoplasm.

Final Answer:
The vegetative cell is larger with abundant food reserves and an irregular nucleus, while the generative cell is small, spindle-shaped, and floats in the vegetative cytoplasm.

answer.text: The vegetative cell is larger with abundant food reserves and an irregular nucleus, whereas the generative cell is smaller, spindle-shaped, and floats in the vegetative cytoplasm
The vegetative cell is small and spindle-shaped, whereas the generative cell is spherical and occupies nearly the entire pollen volume
The vegetative cell lacks any nucleus and serves only for buoyancy, whereas the generative cell is highly vacuolated
Both cells are identical in dimensions, spherical in shape, and separated by a thick sporopollenin septum

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q14 - Structural significance of germ pores on pollen exine

questiontext.text: What is the definitive anatomical characteristic of the germ pores present on the exine of an angiosperm pollen grain?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Although the exine forms a durable, continuous protective coat of sporopollenin, it must allow exit of the emerging pollen tube during germination.

Step 2: Anatomical Definition
Germ pores are precise apertures or round thinnings in the pollen wall where sporopollenin is completely absent, allowing the underlying intine to emerge as the elongating pollen tube.

Final Answer:
Germ pores are regions where sporopollenin is absent.

answer.text: They are thickened regions where both exine and intine are fortified with suberin
They are distinct apertures where sporopollenin deposition is absent
They are specialized sites where the intine is perforated to release enzymes
They are prominent depressions filled with dense pectin and lipid droplets

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q15 - Comparative viability periods among angiosperm pollens

questiontext.text: Regarding the duration of pollen viability, which of the following accurately contrasts cereals such as wheat and rice with members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pollen viability varies markedly among plant families and is strongly modulated by ambient temperature and relative humidity.

Step 2: Family Specificity
In cereal crops like wheat and rice, shed pollen loses viability within about 30 minutes of release. Conversely, in botanical families such as Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae, pollen grains retain their viability for several months under suitable conditions.

Final Answer:
Cereal pollen viability is brief (about 30 minutes), while members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae maintain viability for months.

answer.text: Pollen of rice and wheat remains viable for months, whereas pollen of Rosaceae loses viability within 30 minutes
Pollen of both groups maintains viability for exactly 24 hours under natural field conditions
Pollen of rice and wheat loses viability within 30 minutes, whereas pollen of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae remains viable for months
Pollen of rice and wheat survives for several years, whereas pollen of Solanaceae degrades immediately upon anther opening

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q16 - Cryopreservation parameters for pollen storage

questiontext.text: Pollen grains of numerous agricultural and horticultural species can be stored for long periods in pollen banks by cryopreservation under which temperature condition?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cryopreservation halts all cellular metabolic activities without damaging viability, enabling extended germplasm preservation for breeding programs.

Step 2: Temperature Specification
Pollen grains are stored in liquid nitrogen at its boiling point of \(-196^\circ\text{C}\). This maintains pollen integrity over years, functioning analogously to seed banks in crop improvement initiatives.

Final Answer:
Pollen cryopreservation is conducted in liquid nitrogen at \(-196^\circ\text{C}\).

answer.text: In dry ice at \(-78.5^\circ\text{C}\)

In liquid helium at \(-269^\circ\text{C}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q17 - Contrasting syncarpous and apocarpous gynoecia

questiontext.text: Which of the following pairs of plants correctly exemplifies a multicarpellary syncarpous gynoecium and a multicarpellary apocarpous gynoecium, respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When a flower possesses multiple carpels (multicarpellary), the carpels may either be fused together (syncarpous) or remain free (apocarpous).

Step 2: NCERT Exemplar Evaluation
In Papaver (opium poppy), multiple carpels are completely fused into a single syncarpous compound pistil. In Michelia (champa), numerous separate, free carpels are spirally arranged on an elongated floral axis (apocarpous condition).

Final Answer:
Papaver possesses a syncarpous gynoecium, whereas Michelia possesses an apocarpous gynoecium.

answer.text: Papaver (syncarpous) and Michelia (apocarpous)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q18 - Ovule number variation per ovary across species

questiontext.text: In which of the following groups do all listed plants possess an ovary containing only a single ovule?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The number of ovules borne on the placenta inside an ovarian cavity ranges from exactly one to many thousands depending on the species.

Step 2: Taxon Categorization
Wheat, paddy (rice), and mango each possess an uniovulate ovary (one ovule per ovary). In contrast, papaya, watermelon, and orchids contain multiovulate ovaries with numerous ovules per ovary.

Final Answer:
The group containing a single ovule per ovary is wheat, paddy, and mango.

answer.text: Papaya, watermelon, and orchids

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q19 - Definition of monosporic embryo sac development

questiontext.text: In angiosperms, what does the term 'monosporic development' of the female gametophyte specifically denote?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Megasporogenesis yields a linear tetrad of four haploid megaspores from the diploid megaspore mother cell.

Step 2: Monosporic Ontogeny
In the vast majority of angiosperms (Polygonum type), three megaspores situated towards the micropyle degenerate, leaving only one functional megaspore (typically at the chalazal pole). Because the complete mature 7-celled embryo sac develops exclusively from this single surviving megaspore, the process is called monosporic development.

Final Answer:
Monosporic development refers to embryo sac development from a single functional megaspore.

answer.text: The formation of a single megaspore mother cell from the archesporium

The development of the entire embryo sac from a single functional megaspore, while the other three degenerate

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q20 - Nuclear division nature during embryo sac formation

questiontext.text: During female gametophyte formation, the mitotic nuclear divisions that transform the 2-nucleate stage into the 8-nucleate stage are described as strictly free nuclear because:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mitotic divisions in plants may be followed directly by cytokinesis or proceed as coenocytic/free-nuclear karyokineses.

Step 2: Sequential Behavior in Angiosperms
The nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically to produce 2, 4, and then 8 nuclei without any intervening cytokinesis or cell wall deposition. Only after reaching the 8-nucleate stage are cell walls laid down to organize the cells, making these sequential divisions strictly free nuclear.

Final Answer:
The divisions are free nuclear because nuclear divisions are not followed immediately by cell wall deposition.

answer.text: The nuclei float in external water currents inside the ovarian locule

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q21 - Functional and genetic comparison of geitonogamy

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements correctly evaluates geitonogamy in terms of its ecological mechanism and genetic consequences?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Geitonogamy refers to the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower on the same plant individual.

Step 2: Functional vs Genetic Analysis
Because pollen must move between physically separated flowers, geitonogamy functionally relies on an external pollinating agent (wind, insect, etc.), behaving like cross-pollination. However, because both flowers reside on the same genetically uniform sporophyte, the pollen grains originate from the same genotype, making it genetically equivalent to autogamy.

Final Answer:
Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically equivalent to autogamy.

answer.text: Functionally it represents cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, but genetically it is similar to autogamy
Functionally and genetically it is identical to xenogamy, generating broad allelic diversity
Functionally it is autogamous without pollinators, but genetically it introduces new recombinant alleles
Functionally it is strictly cleistogamous, but genetically it requires two unrelated parental genotypes

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q22 - Adaptations of wind-pollinated flowers

questiontext.text: Which combination of floral traits is typically observed in anemophilous (wind-pollinated) angiosperms, such as grasses and maize?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Anemophily depends on passive aerial dispersion to convey male gametophytes to receptive female organs.

Step 2: Trait Adaptation
To maximize aerodynamic dispersion and aerial capture, wind-pollinated plants produce dry, light, non-sticky pollen in large quantities. Their stamens are well-exposed to air currents, and their stigmas are large and feathery (as seen in corn cob silks) to effectively trap airborne grains.

Final Answer:
Wind-pollinated flowers have light, non-sticky pollen, well-exposed stamens, and large feathery stigmas.

answer.text: Heavy, sticky pollen grains coated with nectar, brightly colored perianth, and sunken stigmas
Light and non-sticky pollen grains, well-exposed stamens, and large feathery stigmas

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q23 - Hydrophily mechanisms in Vallisneria and Zostera

Hydrophily is restricted to about 30 genera (mostly monocots) and operates either at the water surface (epihydrophily) or completely submerged (hypohydrophily).

Step 2: Comparative Mode
In Vallisneria, female flowers reach the water surface on elongated coiled stalks; male flowers or pollens float passively on the surface until contacting the stigma. In marine seagrasses like Zostera, female flowers remain submerged, and long, ribbon-like pollen grains protected by mucilage are transported inside the water column.

Final Answer:
Vallisneria pollinates on the water surface, whereas Zostera releases ribbon-like pollen that travels submerged inside water.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q24 - Pollination mode in water hyacinth and water lily

In water hyacinth and water lily, flowers emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q25 - Mutualistic floral rewards in Yucca and Amorphophallus

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q26 - Breeding outcome of monoecious condition in maize and castor

Monoecy describes the separation of male and female reproductive structures into unisexual flowers on a single plant sporophyte.

Because an individual flower contains only stamens or only carpels, pollen cannot land on the stigma of that exact same flower, thereby preventing autogamy. However, pollen from a staminate flower can readily be transferred to a pistillate flower on the same plant, allowing geitonogamy to occur.

Monoecy prevents autogamy but does not prevent geitonogamy.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q27 - Mechanism of self-incompatibility in plants

questiontext.text: How does the genetic outbreeding device termed self-incompatibility prevent inbreeding depression in angiosperms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Self-incompatibility is an active physiological recognition barrier between the pollen grain and the tissues of the pistil.

Step 2: Cellular Action
When pollen from the same flower or another flower of the same plant lands on the stigma, genetically controlled chemical interactions trigger rejection. The pistil halts either pollen germination on the stigma surface or retards pollen tube elongation through the style, thereby preventing self-fertilisation.

Final Answer:
Self-incompatibility prevents self-fertilisation by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q28 - Emasculation protocol in unisexual female parents

Emasculation is defined as the surgical removal of anthers from a flower bud before dehiscence to prevent self-pollination.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q29 - Adaptive significance of endosperm preceding embryo

questiontext.text: In post-fertilisation events of angiosperms, endosperm development typically precedes embryo development. What is the adaptive significance of this timing?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Following double fertilisation, the zygote undergoes a period of rest while the primary endosperm cell immediately initiates division.

Step 2: Physiological Justification
The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly to build a cellular tissue rich in reserve carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids. Final Answer:
Endosperm development precedes embryogeny to ensure assured nutrition for the developing embryo.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q31 - Classification of non-albuminous and albuminous seeds

Seeds are classified based on whether residual endosperm persists in the mature seed or is entirely utilized during embryogenesis.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q32 - Definition and occurrences of perisperm

In black pepper (Piper nigrum) and beet (Beta vulgaris), portions of the diploid nucellar tissue survive into the mature seed as a persistent, nutritive layer located outside the embryo sac, termed perisperm.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q33 - Structural features of a grass embryo
